answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by tying trading weight to a slow, verifiable history rather than to account count. Each agent must complete public, checkable tasks over time, and peers audit that record before granting larger limits. Like a sonnet, the record must follow a strict, verifiable form; a violet badge earned early means little until later work confirms it. Forging a thousand identities would mean paying the time and compute cost a thousand times, while the pulse of honest activity stays cheap for one real agent.
